### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 formed a three-way choice that ran in almost every trace: A19 appeared in about 37 in 100 traces (73 of 200), A20 in about 31 (62) and A25 in about 35 (70), while any two of them rarely ran in the same trace (about 1 in 100 or fewer). In the later window, A20 and A25 appear in no trace and A19 in a single trace. [OCC018, OCC019, OCC024, REL001, REL003, REL008]
- These three activities sat between A41 and A26: in the earlier window, every trace containing one of them also contained A41 before it and A26 after it (for example, A41 preceded A19 in all of A19's traces, and A19 preceded A26 in about 35 of its 36–37 traces per 100), with A31 further downstream. In the later window, A41, A26 and A31 still occur in essentially every trace, but without any of the three. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, OCC036, POS005, POS006]
- A41's outgoing transitions changed accordingly: in the earlier window about 87 in 100 led to A19 (about 29), A20 (about 26) or A25 (about 32); in the later window about 86 in 100 lead straight to A26, and transitions into A19, A20 or A25 are no longer observed. [DIR041, DIR019, DIR020, DIR025]
- The A41→A26 distance within a trace shortened from mostly two event positions (about 85 in 100 observed pairs; three positions in about 15) to mostly one position (about 86 in 100), and A26's mean position moved slightly earlier (about 0.39 to 0.37 of the trace length). [LAG003, POS005]
- Some routing shares between existing alternatives elsewhere also moved: A12 now leads to A14 in about 42 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 26 before) and to A11 in about 20 (about 39 before); A21 leads to A24 in about 35 in 100 (about 14 before); A24 leads to A31 in about 58 in 100 (about 38 before). [DIR012, DIR021, DIR024]
- Participation shifted moderately for several other activities — down by roughly 4–10 in 100 traces for A01, A02, A05, A07, A09, A10, A21 and A23, up by roughly 4–10 for A03, A06, A11, A12, A13, A17, A22 and A24 — and A15 and A16, which run in every trace, repeat somewhat more often (A15 recurs in about 34 in 100 traces versus about 27). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the three-way choice between the alternative activities A19, A20 and A25, which previously executed between A41 and A26 in almost every earlier trace, is no longer made, so that in the later window A41 leads directly on to A26. In the earlier window each trace ran exactly one of the three (roughly a third of traces each, in a fixed order A41 before and A26 after the chosen activity), while in the later window the three are observed at most once in 200 traces, A41's outgoing transitions go to A26 in about 86 in 100 cases, and the A41→A26 lag dropped from mostly two positions to one. This reading is shown directly by the successor change at A41 and the shortened lag, and it is consistent across the occurrence, relation, position and lag indicators, with the key items all highly unusual for random re-splits of the two windows. [DIR041, LAG003, OCC018, OCC019, OCC024, REL004, REL006, REL009, REL016, REL019, POS001, POS002, POS004]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A19, A20 and A25 still execute but have become very rare: zero participation only means they were not observed in the 200 later traces (A19 still appears once), so a drastic drop in how often paths containing them are taken cannot be separated from a full removal. The evidence also provides no baseline for how many small shifts an unchanged process would produce, so the secondary routing and participation differences may partly be sampling variation. [OCC018, OCC019, OCC024]

Other differences:
- Routing among the existing alternatives A11, A12, A13 and A14 — all still present in about half of traces in both windows — shifted: A12 leads to A14 in about 42 in 100 of its outgoing transitions versus about 26 before and to A11 in about 20 versus about 39; A03 leads less often to A12 (about 26 versus 40) and more often to A11 (about 38 versus 29); A13 leads less often to A14 (about 28 versus 42). This pattern is consistent with existing paths being taken with different frequencies. [DIR003, DIR012, DIR013, OCC003, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013]
- Around A21, A22, A23, A24 and A31 the shares also moved: A21 leads to A24 in about 35 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 14 before) and less often to A31 (about 38 versus 54); A24 leads to A31 in about 58 in 100 (about 38 before) and less often to A21 (about 15 versus 28); A23 leads more often to A22 (about 27 versus 16); A24's participation rose from about 50 to 56 in 100 traces and it now co-occurs with A26 in about 56 in 100 traces versus about 50. [DIR021, DIR023, DIR024, OCC023, REL013]
- Participation shifted by roughly 4–10 in 100 traces for several further activities (down: A01, A02, A05, A07, A09, A10, A37, A40; up: A06, A17, A22, A35, A36), and A15 and A16 repeat somewhat more often (A15 recurs in about 34 in 100 traces versus about 27; A16 about 33 versus 27). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC009, OCC010, OCC017, OCC020, OCC021, OCC030, OCC031, OCC032, OCC035, OCC015, OCC016]
